items.title: The 1931 Yangtze flood killed millions
items.claim: What was the death toll of the 1931 China floods?

options.text: Around 100,000 — comparable to other major river floods
Estimates range from 422,000 to over 4 million dead — likely the deadliest natural disaster of the 20th century

items.reveal:
The 1931 floods affected the Yangtze, Huai and Yellow river basins after extreme monsoon rainfall. Chris Courtney's 'The Nature of Disaster in China' (2018) places direct deaths from drowning at around 150,000 and total deaths including disease and famine at perhaps 2 million; older estimates went higher.

Wuhan was submerged for weeks. The Republic of China government's response was overwhelmed by the simultaneous Mukden Incident (September 1931, Japanese invasion of Manchuria).
items.why: River flooding remains the deadliest natural hazard category by long-term death toll. Vulnerability is not just about hazard — it's about state capacity, infrastructure and political moment.

items.title: The boreal forest is the world's largest terrestrial biome
items.claim: Which is the world's largest forest biome?

options.text: The boreal forest (taiga) — a circumpolar belt across Russia, Canada, Alaska and Scandinavia totalling around 1.5 billion hectares; larger than all tropical rainforests combined and storing more carbon

items.reveal:
Boreal forest covers around 30% of all forest area and stores an estimated 30-40% of terrestrial carbon — much of it in deep peat and permafrost soils. Russia's taiga alone is around 12 million km².

Dominant species: spruce, fir, pine, larch, birch. Wildlife: brown bear, lynx, wolverine, capercaillie, moose. Productivity per hectare is lower than the Amazon, but the area is far larger.

Climate change is intensifying boreal wildfires — Siberia 2019-21, Canada 2023 — releasing carbon and potentially turning some boreal regions into net carbon sources. Permafrost thaw could release vast methane and CO₂.
items.why: The Amazon dominates public attention as 'the lungs of the planet'. The boreal forest is larger, stores more carbon, and is increasingly fire-prone — but receives a fraction of the press coverage.

items.title: The jet stream sits around 10 km above the surface

options.text: A surface wind near the equator
A narrow band of fast westerly winds (often 100-300 km/h) at around 9-12 km altitude (the tropopause), driven by temperature contrasts between polar and tropical air masses
An ocean current in the Pacific
A jet of supersonic air over deserts

items.reveal:
The polar jet (UK weather) and subtropical jet are the major Northern Hemisphere features. They meander in Rossby waves, and the shape of those waves controls where storm systems track.

Jet streams were discovered by Japanese balloon-bombing campaigns of WWII and by US bomber crews over the Pacific (1944) flying west into apparently impossible headwinds.

Arctic amplification (warming of the Arctic at roughly 4x the global rate) reduces the temperature contrast that drives the polar jet, possibly causing it to meander more — linked to more persistent weather extremes.
items.why: Surface weather has upper-atmosphere causes. Understanding why summer 2022 had heat domes or 2013-14 had stuck storm tracks requires looking at the jet.
